change.title: fix(acp): attach MCP servers when a chat is reopened outside Reload
change.description: > Dibuat oleh Termul Dev (bot). ## Summary A chat reopened through any path other than **Reload this chat** (idle-stop auto-resume, manual Resume chat, opening a past chat from history onto a fresh process) resumed the ACP session with `mcpServers: undefined`. On the wire that means the host runs `prepare_reopen_mcp` with `None`, so the reopened agent gets no user-configured MCP servers **and no Termul host plan server**. `mcp__termul__*` (canvas, `plan`, `set_session_title`, `ask_user`) and every configured server vanish mid-conversation (#1420). Only `reloadAgentChat` built a list; `openHistorySession` forwarded `options?.mcpServers`, which is `undefined` for every other caller (`use-idle-stop-auto-resume.ts` calls `openHistorySession(sessionId)` with no options). ## Related Issue Closes #1420 Prior art searched (open and closed): #1436 (closed by the retired automation routine, not on review merit; same idea, never merged). Open draft #908 (`fix(acp): restart Devin after terminal login and send MCP on reopen`) overlaps: it also makes `session.ts` pass an MCP list to `loadSession`/`resumeSession` (via a `mcpServersForReopen` helper, positional args on an older base) and also touches `acp-transport` types, `agent.ts`, and Rust `acp/manager`. It is based on an older `dev` and its signatures no longer match (`dev` now has `reopenRoots` plus `options?.mcpServers`), so the two will conflict textually in `slices/session.ts`. This PR is scoped to the renderer default only; whichever lands second needs a rebase and the redundant helper can be dropped. ## Type of Change - [x] fix: bug fix - [x] test: adds or updates tests ## What Changed - `src/renderer/stores/acp-store/slices/session.ts`: in `openHistorySessionInner`, once the live agent and its capabilities are resolved, default the reopen MCP list to `selectMcpServersForAgent(get().mcpServers, capabilities).servers` when the caller omits it (`options?.mcpServers ??`). An explicit list (Reload this chat) still wins. The three `loadSession`/`resumeSession` calls send the resolved list. Added a renderer boundary log (`acp.openHistorySession.mcpAttach`) with session id and server count only (no server names, commands, URLs or tokens). - Doc comments updated to the new contract: `ReopenCallOptions` (`src/renderer/lib/acp-transport/types.ts`) and `OpenHistoryOptions` (`src/renderer/stores/acp-store/types.ts`). - Rust, old plan token (review fix): `prepare_reopen_mcp` (`src-tauri/src/acp/manager/mod.rs`) used to call `unregister_session` BEFORE the reopen was sent, so a failed reopen left a still-live agent child holding a token the host no longer knew, and it could not call `plan`. Now the session's earlier token stays valid while the reopen is in flight. `load_session` and `resume_session` settle it afterwards through the new `HostPlanServer::settle_reopen_token` (`src-tauri/src/acp/host_mcp/parent.rs`): on success the session's other tokens and per-session state are dropped (what the old code did, just later) and the new token is kept; on failure only the new token is evicted, and the old token, the plan cache and the title flags are left alone. `unregister_by_token` is not used on that path because it also drops the bound session's plan cache. `None` still means no MCP list and no token work. If the MCP gate rejects the list, the new token is evicted through the same failure path (`settle_reopen_token(.., false)`), so the old token, the plan cache and the title flags survive there too (a first version used `unregister_by_token` there, which also dropped the plan cache; fixed in the second review round). `load_session` and `resume_session` now look up the agent's command channel BEFORE `prepare_reopen_mcp` registers a token, so that lookup can no longer return early and leave a new token registered. - Rust tests (`host_mcp/parent/tests.rs`): a failed reopen keeps the old token valid (a real `plan` call over the loopback bridge succeeds) and evicts the new one (rejected); a failed reopen keeps the plan cache and title flag; a successful reopen drops the old token (rejected) and keeps the new one (accepted); other sessions' tokens are untouched; a first-time reopen with no earlier token keeps the new one. - Rust tests (`manager/tests.rs`, through `resume_session` on the test agents): a gate-rejected MCP list (HTTP server, agent without HTTP support) leaves the old token and the plan cache; a failed resume keeps the old token and the plan cache and leaves exactly one token; a successful resume leaves exactly one token and it is a new one; a reopen with `None` touches no token. Not covered by a test: the early return of `command_tx` (an unknown agent already fails at the capability lookup before any token exists, so that order is a code-level guarantee only). - Tests: new test in `history-session.test.ts` that an `openHistorySession(id)` with no options (what idle-stop auto-resume does) sends a non-`undefined` `mcpServers` carrying the configured server on `acp_resume_session`. Six existing exact-payload assertions in `history-session.test.ts` / `persistence.test.ts` now include `mcpServers: []` (empty registry), reflecting the corrected behavior. Not changed, known follow-up: `openDiscoveredSession` (agent-native sessions found through `session/list`) still calls `loadSession`/`resumeSession` with no MCP list. History: it was written in #407/#415, before the reopen MCP list existed (#1226 added the list only for Reload this chat); no comment or test says the omission is deliberate, and no test asserts an MCP list for it. It looks like an oversight, but it is a different path (sessions Termul did not create, so registering a plan token for them is a product decision), so it is left out of this PR's scope. Reviewers: please confirm whether that path should also attach, then it can be a separate PR. ## How It Was Tested - [x] `bun run ci` (Biome lint + format + imports, strict mode) - [x] `bun run typecheck` - [x] `bun run test` - [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (in src-tauri) - [x] `cargo test` (in src-tauri): targeted `cargo test --lib -- acp::host_mcp acp::manager`, not the whole suite - [ ] Manual verification completed - [ ] Not applicable Results, run on a Linux box with Node 20.19.2 / Bun 1.4.2: - `bun run ci`: pass. `bun run typecheck` (node, web, test): pass. - `bun run test`: 10390 passed, 11 failed in 5 files. All 11 fail with `Promise.withResolvers is not a function` (Node 20 lacks it; none are in files this PR touches). Re-running those 5 files with `bun --bun x vitest run ...`: 143/143 passed. - Focused: `history-session.test.ts`, `persistence.test.ts`, `reload-chat.test.ts`, `AgentChatPanel.test.tsx` (uses the idle-stop hook): 206 passed. - Rust (review fix commit), on Linux: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` in `src-tauri`: pass. `cargo test --lib -- acp::host_mcp acp::manager`: 319 passed, 0 failed (includes the 5 token tests in `host_mcp` and 4 in `manager`). Second review round: same commands, same result. The full `cargo test --lib` was not re-run for this commit; the only two failures known on clean `dev` are the network-only `acp::browser_shim::tests::loopback_validation_accepts_loopback_forms` and `ssh::connect::tests::unresolvable_host_is_a_dns_failure`. - Not verified: no live agent. The token tests drive `HostPlanServer` directly and do not run a real `load_session`/`resume_session` against an agent process, so the wiring in the manager (the `outcome.is_ok()` branch) is covered by review and by the compiler, not by a test. Not manually verified in the desktop app (idle-stop, then a canvas tool call). Behavior to check in review: a history open that adopts an already-live idle agent now also sends `Some(list)`, so the host registers a new plan token for that session (same as Reload does). The old token is dropped only if the reopen succeeds. **Not verified (idle or adopted agent keeps its old plan child):** the host only forwards the list in `session/load` / `session/resume`; what the agent does with `mcpServers` for a session it already holds is agent-specific and I could not verify it from this code or run a live agent. If an agent keeps its OLD `termul` stdio child after a successful reopen instead of starting the new one, that child still carries the old token, which is dropped on success, so its `plan` / canvas / title calls would be rejected as `auth rejected` until the agent is restarted. The host has a repair path for retained children (`process_request` re-routes a known token bound to an older session when the agent has one active turn), but it needs the token to still be known, so it does not cover this case. This risk is not new in kind: before this PR, Reload dropped the old token before the reopen as well. I did not change this behavior and do not claim it is handled. If it turns out to matter, keeping earlier tokens until the session closes would cover it (`unregister_session` already removes every token bound to a session). ## Screenshots or Recordings N/A (no UI change). ## CI & Review Gate - [ ] All CI checks pass (PR Validation, Rust Checks, Build Verification, Security Scans) - [ ] Code review comments from CodeRabbit / Claude have been addressed or resolved - [ ] No unresolved review findings remain Opened as a draft: CI and review have not run yet. The renderer and targeted Rust checks were run locally (see above). ## Checklist - [x] My PR title follows the conventional commit format used by this repo - [x] I linked the related issue or explained why none exists - [x] I updated docs when needed - [x] I added or updated tests when needed - [x] I verified the change does not introduce unrelated modifications - [x] I read AGENTS.md and followed the contributor guidelines - [ ] A human reviewed the complete diff before submission --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes chats reopened outside "Reload this chat" (idle-stop auto-resume, manual Resume, history-row opens) losing the host `termul` plan server and every configured MCP server mid-conversation (#1420). The reopen MCP list now defaults to the user's configured servers when the caller omits it; Reload's explicit list still wins. - Adds an info-level boundary log with session id and server count only, never server names, commands, URLs, or tokens. - Adds a test for the no-options reopen path; existing payload assertions now expect `mcpServers: []`. - Updates doc comments in the store and transport types plus the `prepare_reopen_mcp` Rust doc (no Rust behavior change). - `openDiscoveredSession` is intentionally unchanged; it reopens on an already-connected agent. Written for commit d1256ff2803336db4227eb2488d214e42cf70b8a. Summary will update on new commits. --- Keputusan CEO (25 Okt 2026): token plan lama tetap dihapus setelah reopen sukses, dan `openDiscoveredSession` tidak diubah di PR ini (issue lanjutan akan dibuka Triage). Perilaku agent idle yang diadopsi tetap belum terverifikasi.

commits.message:
fix(acp): attach MCP servers when a chat is reopened outside Reload (#1420)

Idle-stop auto-resume, manual Resume chat and history-row opens called
openHistorySession without an mcpServers list, so session/load and
session/resume reached the host with None and the agent lost the host
termul server and every configured MCP server. Default the list to
selectMcpServersForAgent(state.mcpServers, capabilities).servers when the
caller omits it; an explicit list (Reload this chat) still wins.

fix(acp): drop the old plan token only after a reopen succeeds (#1420)

prepare_reopen_mcp removed the session's earlier plan token before the
reopen was sent. A failed reopen left a still-live agent child unable to
call plan. The earlier token now stays valid until load_session or
resume_session succeeds, then HostPlanServer::settle_reopen_token drops
it and keeps the new one. On failure only the new token is evicted, and
the session's plan cache and per-session state are left alone.

fix(acp): evict only the new plan token when the MCP gate rejects a reopen (#1420)

The gate rejection path used unregister_by_token, which also drops the
bound session's plan cache. It now takes the failure path of
settle_reopen_token, so the earlier token and the session state stay.

load_session and resume_session resolve the command channel before
prepare_reopen_mcp registers a token, so that lookup cannot leave one
behind. Add manager-level tests for the gate rejection, a failed resume,
a successful resume and a reopen without an MCP list.
